findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The cap arithmetic is not disputed. Rent of GBP 1300 per calendar month gives annual rent of GBP 15,600, so the five-week cap is GBP 1,500.00, and the stated deposit of GBP 1,500 is exactly at the cap and not above it. The amount is therefore compliant if the cap applies. The jurisdiction ("unknown"), the tenancy type ("unknown") and the rent basis ("unknown") are all unconfirmed in the context. The contract does not say the property is in England, though the address is in London. It also does not confirm that this is an ordinary private tenancy, or that the rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. No quoted text defeats the interpretation, so dismissal is unsupported, and the issue stays conditional on those facts. A compliant amount says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

questions: Is this a private tenancy in England with the landlord living elsewhere?
What rent period and tenancy does the deposit cover, and can the amount be revised?

expectations.explanation: message_checker:pose_as_buyer quotes the exact concealment instruction and is suspicious with critical severity. But it is filed under payment_safety, not right_to_let, and its detail frames it as a payment/identity misdescription ('label the payment as friends and family'). That does not match the expected right_to_let concern about concealment, so I cannot resolve whether the semantic expectation is met. The related finding no_checks_needed sits under right_to_let but quotes the owner-not-letting line and not the buyer-pretence line.

message_checker:no_checks_needed is a suspicious right_to_let finding quoting 'No, the owner is only selling. I will give you a tenancy under their name anyway.' Its detail says the owner does not know about the letting and so there is no right to grant a tenancy. That matches the expected owner-not-letting concern. The title ('No references, contract or checks needed') is a poor fit for the content, but the semantics are right.

forbidden_assertions.explanation: No output says the sale listing alone proves fraud. The right_to_let finding relies on the admission that the owner is unaware of the letting, not on the sale listing.

No output says a buyer viewing verifies letting authority. act_viewing asks for an in-person viewing before payment, and it is not framed as proof of authority. The right_to_let check stays suspicious.

unsupported_claims.output_quote: Genuine landlords must check your right to rent and normally want references and a contract. Skipping all of this suggests the person may not be able to let the property.
unsupported_claims.explanation: The chat contains no statement that references or checks are skipped. The case also includes a tenancy agreement. Only the owner-unaware admission supports the finding, so this part of the detail is boilerplate and not grounded in the evidence.

unsupported_claims.output_quote: or to label the payment as friends and family. That removes the payment protection you would otherwise have.
unsupported_claims.explanation: The chat has no payment or friends-and-family request. This detail is template text that does not match the evidence.

unsupported_claims.output_quote: £1,300 a month against roughly £950 for a room in W12 (approximate area figure): about 37% higher.
unsupported_claims.explanation: The £950 area figure has no supplied source. It is loosely hedged, but it is an unsupported comparison. The evidence_id 'listing' is also non-standard, though it matched structurally.

grounding_issues.explanation: The quote '£1,300 pcm' is only a structured rendering of the listing rent. It supports the rent figure but not the claimed area average, and no source for the £950 benchmark is in the input or the controlled records.

The quote is exact. However, the finding's interpretation (payment misdescription, friends-and-family labelling) is not what the quoted text says. The quote is about concealing a rental purpose from the selling agent.

grading.reviewer_note: The controlled selling_agent_record says Mira Vale is selling and has not authorised Rowan Pike to advertise a tenancy. None of the outputs used it. The outputs also left the decision null with an unchanged score of 100 and set no hard flag, despite two suspicious findings. The outputs include no question about the owner's consent to let, though the message_checker question asks about proof of authority. Expectation 0 is marked indeterminate because the concealment finding is filed under payment_safety, not right_to_let.
